# Results — Study 78 (Crossed-Wires) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — MACD(12,26,9)
signal-line crossover on daily bars, enter at the next bar's open **in the direction of the
cross**, exit on a symmetric take-profit/stop of **±1 ATR(20)**, max-hold 60 days — run across
a basket of six liquid instruments (SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL, TSLA, NVDA) and pinned against a
**random-direction control** on the *same* entries. As-of **2026-06-12**; Yahoo daily bars
(5-year history via `period="5y"`). Trades pooled across the basket: **n = 581** (~97/instrument).*

## The honest test — symmetric ±1 ATR, gross (cost = 0)

A direction-symmetric payoff is the only fair way to ask *"does the cross point the right way?"*
— with TP and SL equidistant, a coin earns ≈ 0.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **MACD cross (with the cross)** | 581 | **52.5%** | **+12.65** | −0.13 | **+0.94** |
| Random direction (control) | 581 | 48.9% | −2.02 | — | −0.17 |

- The crossover's gross expectancy is **+12.65 bps/trade** at HAC *t* = **+0.94** — statistically
  **indistinguishable from zero**. The inference bar requires |*t*| ≥ 2; this falls well short.
- Cross − random = **+14.67 bps/trade**: the MACD direction does appear to slightly edge a coin,
  but the signal is too noisy across only ~97 trades per instrument to be trusted. This is
  **WEAK** at best — consistent with noise, not evidence of a real edge.
- Per-instrument, no tape carries a real edge: every HAC |*t*| < 1.1 (SPY −0.64, QQQ +0.79,
  IWM +0.66, AAPL +0.31, TSLA +1.01, NVDA −0.06). TSLA is the loudest at +1.01 — still well
  short.

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep

The MACD on daily bars fires **~97 times per instrument over five years**, or roughly **19 times
per year** (much lower turnover than Study 72's ~11/day SMA scalp). Even at 5 bps the
per-trade mean stays positive *in point estimate*, but the HAC t-stat never clears 1:

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +12.65 | +0.94 | well below inference bar |
| 0.5 bps | +12.15 | +0.90 | |
| 1.0 bps | +11.65 | +0.86 | |
| 2.0 bps | +10.65 | +0.79 | |
| 5.0 bps | +7.65 | +0.57 | |

The low turnover means costs don't kill this the way they killed Study 72 — but the signal
never clears the inference bar in the first place, so costs are irrelevant: there is nothing
to erode. **MIRAGE**: you cannot trade a noise signal.

## The fixed-tick trap

| Exit rule | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Symmetric 1:1 (honest) | 52.5% | +12.65 | −0.13 | +0.94 |
| TP 0.5R / SL 2R (1:4) | 78.5% | −22.46 | −2.34 | −1.58 |
| TP 0.25R / "no stop" (8R) | **95.2%** | −26.39 | **−6.98** | −1.25 |

Note: unlike Study 72 (SMA scalp), the "no-stop" arm here actually *hurts* the positive
gross mean — the daily MACD's positive drift comes from the symmetric side, not the
fixed-tick side. The win-rate illusion is present (95% wins) but the mean goes negative,
confirming the high-win-rate is pure exit geometry, not forecasting.

## Forward return horizons (d5, d20, d60)

| Horizon | MACD cross mean | MACD *t* | Random mean | Random *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5 days | −3.37 bps | −0.20 | +15.47 bps | +0.92 |
| 20 days | +29.65 bps | +1.03 | −8.61 bps | −0.18 |
| 60 days | +28.78 bps | +0.83 | +9.15 bps | +0.12 |

The forward returns are inconsistent across horizons and noisy: at d5 the cross actually
underperforms a coin; at d20/d60 it outperforms but neither t-stat clears the inference bar.
This inconsistency is the signature of noise, not a persistent signal.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same MACD engine
recovers a crossover edge only when bar-level momentum is planted, and reads ≈ 0 when it
isn't — confirming the indicator is a faithful momentum harvester, and that the real tape
simply lacks persistent trend structure at the MACD's horizon:

| Planted bar AR(1) momentum | MACD cross gross (bps/trade) | beats random control? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.10 (persistence) | positive | yes |
| −0.10 (reversion) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Gross HAC *t* = +0.94 (right sign, but below the |*t*| ≥ 2 inference bar).
  The cross + random delta of +14.67 bps is directionally consistent with a real effect but too
  noisy (~97 trades/instrument) to confirm. Literature suggests MACD "works" in some historical
  studies but those relied on longer histories and survivorship-biased universes.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A WEAK signal that never clears inference is untradable regardless
  of cost. The low turnover (~19 trades/yr) spares costs, but a noise signal cannot be traded
  at any scale.
- **Beats a coin? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The +14.67 bps delta vs the coin is directionally positive
  but statistically indistinguishable from zero at this sample size.
